messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — rethinking where we run heavy bench vs light smoke in the model onboarding flow. Right now full bench runs in the ingest path and it's creating a long critical path for new models.
Devon Park: +1. That blocks quick experiments. Proposal: split into two phases: a fast runtime-compat smoke (<=10s) on the ingest path that returns a small pass/fail + fingerprint, and an async full bench that runs in the bench service and publishes detailed metrics.
Eli Gómez: Sounds good. How do we keep guarantees? We need a clear manifest contract so the smoke can sanity-check the runtime without needing the full bench inputs.
Maya Chen: Idea: minimal model_metadata.json emitted with upload that includes arch, tokenization hints, small perf expectations and 'smoke_probes' pointers. Example sketch:
```json
{
  "name": "mymodel-v1",
  "arch": "llama2-13b",
  "input_shapes": [[1, 512]],
  "tokenizer": "sentencepiece",
  "expected_latency_ms": 120,
  "smoke_probes": ["small_prompt_set_v1"],
  "quantized_variants": ["int8", "nf4"]
}
```
Devon Park: Nice. Boundary surfaces: ingest only needs (model_uri, model_metadata.json, uploader_id). Bench needs full artifact uri, datasets, and policy flags. Keep the ingest manifest tiny so we don't blow up the fast path.
Eli Gómez: Also add an explicit enum for compatibility flags, e.g. "compatibility_flags": ["kv-cache-ok","quantize-safe"] and an `acceptance_level` field (auto, manual) so the registry can auto-approve low-risk uploads.
Maya Chen: Tradeoffs to call out in the RFC: false positives in smoke will block good models; false negatives will let broken models reach users. We can mitigate by making smoke checks conservative (quick KV cache probe, one short generation, tokenizer roundtrip) and by storing smoke artifacts for repro.
Devon Park: Operationally we should propagate a trace_id through ingest -> bench so failures are traceable. Also attach a cost_budget tag to uploads so bench scheduler can throttle expensive runs.
infra-bot: infra-bot: Created INF-4221: "onboard: trace propagation + bench quota enforcement" (assignee: @Devon Park)
Maya Chen: Next actions: I'll open an RFC PR describing the ingest/bench interface + sample schema. Eli — can you prototype the smoke harness (target 3 probes, <10s total)? Devon — can you add the minimal contract fields to the registry schema and the fast_accept flag for internal models?
Eli Gómez: :thumbsup: I'll prototype the harness this week. Plan: 1) load model binary smoke (warm), 2) short gen (<=16 tokens) to test kv-cache and attention, 3) tokenizer encode/decode roundtrip.
Devon Park: I'll add `fast_accept` boolean and `smoke_snapshot` storage to the registry. Also propose we default canary rollouts to prefer the non-quantized variant and fallback to quantized variants if perf/cost thresholds are exceeded.
Maya Chen: Good. Also we should keep a reproducible `smoke_snapshot` (prompts + RNG seed + env) attached to the model in the registry so bench can replay identical inputs for debugging.
Eli Gómez: Related note: linking draft doc: https://redwood.internal/notes/onboard-smoke-probes — will update with harness plan.
Maya Chen: If no objections I'll PR the RFC by EOD Friday.
Devon Park: No objections from me.
